This changes friendship from an incidental reward into the social inducement attached to substitution, alongside a territorial pressure with a different immediate result.

findings.title: Messenger continuity and local affiliation
findings.claim: The focus's proposed fabrication and intimate affiliation meet 17:77's line of earlier messengers and its unchanged way. In the HFT reading, accepting the local relationship would move the bearer out of that messenger pattern and into local patronage, changing a message-integrity reading into a question of the bearer's place in a continuing line.
findings.mechanism: The focus disclosure, fabricated attribution, replacement, and intimate-companion carriers meet the context's followed way, messengers sent before, and denied transformation. That contact makes local intimacy a possible alternative affiliation to the messenger line, while the supplied connection places 17:77 after the pressure sequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can notice that the proposed change concerns the bearer and the relationship that would claim him as well as the content of the message.
findings.containment: The move from message replacement to exit from a messenger pattern is the HFT reader's attributed inference. A live alternative is that 17:77 governs the expulsion outcome in 17:76 and does not retroactively qualify the content bargain in 17:73.

epistemic.reason: The supplied 17:77 carriers and focus returns agree, but applying the closing messenger pattern specifically to the intimacy bargain is inferential and remains contested within the packet.

findings.title: The counterfactual cost of inclination
findings.claim: The intimacy offered as the result in 17:73 is placed beside a different consequence in the immediate sequence: 17:74 describes a prevented near-inclination, and 17:75 projects double punishment and no helper if that inclination had occurred. The promised bond is therefore not presented as secure protection.
findings.mechanism: The focus near-action and intimate-companion carriers contact 17:74's near-inclination and stabilization, then 17:75's consequence of double punishment and lack of a helper. This changes the friendship clause from a self-contained reward into one side of a counterfactual whose other side carries severe cost and no divine support.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold the promised social intimacy beside the next ayah's warning about the cost of even slight inclination, without mistaking the imagined bond for protection that was received.
findings.containment: The connection records nominate this relation, and the supplied Arabic gives the consequence text; target morphology for 17:75 is not supplied. The sequence remains hypothetical, and it does not equate the promised human friendship with actual divine support or punishment experienced.

epistemic.reason: The context text and connection records are supplied, but the relation is a bounded interpretation of their sequence; no source trust label is attached to the connection rows.
